**Eval runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-su
ites` | Author-only: create a suite + its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it;
responds `201` + `suiteId`. Each test's case body is an ordered `steps` array (prompt / toolCall / interact / assert); per-test `m
odel`/`provider`/`runs` are optional and fall back to suite defaults |\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (re
run; `serverIds` optional — defaults to the suite's saved servers) or `suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `env
ironmentId` (requires `suiteId`) runs against one of the suite's attached environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PAT
CH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}` | Edit suite settings, including `environmentIds` — the project environments the suite runs against
(non-empty array sets/replaces, `null` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `e
nvironmentId` pins which environment they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary — poll until t
erminal. Carries `gateWaiver`: the audited override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate`
| The stored suite quality-gate report for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` i
s a 200 report, never a missing route. A deployment that predates the evaluator answers `422 FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` |\n| `GET .../
eval-runs/{runId}/decision-summary` | **Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision contract: the verdict and
where it came from, counts labelled with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and per-trial diagnostics wit
h the user-value chain, the first failed stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and one next action (paginate
d) |\n| `POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (required, future,
max 30 days out), with a `reason` (required, max 500 chars). Manage tier. Does NOT change the run's `result` — the run keeps its
verdict and the waiver is reported alongside it. `409` when one is already in force, returning the existing waiver |\n| `GET .../e
val-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | The waiver in force over a run, or `null`. Readable by anyone who can view the run |\n| `DELETE .
../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers/{waiverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putting the gate back. Idempotent — a second call reports the ori
ginal revocation rather than restamping it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations` | Per-iteration results: tool calls, token
usage, latency (paginated) |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/{iterationId}/trace` | Full trace: messages + expected-vs-ac

tual analysis |
| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite, newest first |

**Eval result ingestion** (`/
projects/{projectId}/eval-ingest/...`) — how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves results from eval runs executed outside the platform (local dev,
CI). The `{projectId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the key org's Default project. Most users never call these direct
ly — set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:\n\n| Endpoint | Wha

t it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run from finished results and finalize it |
| `POST
.../eval-ingest/runs/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/run
s/iterations` | Append an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked run (ide
mpotent) |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send inline) and return
its `storageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_UPGRADE_R
EQUIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |\n\n**Agent** (`/projec
ts/{projectId}/agent`) — a headless assistant turn for\nbuilding conversational surfaces (the MCPJam Slack app is the first consum

er):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: "u
ser\"\\|\"assistant\", content}` items, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to t
he project. The turn can read project servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs — kick those off yours
elf with `POST .../eval-runs`. Responds synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links),
and token `usage`. Capped at 4 concurrent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent — never blind-retry**:
dedupe on your own trigger identity, and on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list s

uites) before retrying, or you'll create duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it
does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../studies` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\
n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environm
ent it publishes, and its insights envelope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, n

ever null |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Swarms and User Testing are enabled per organization.** Everything in the
> four sections below
is behind that gate, enforced server-side. If it is not\n> on for your organization, the reads generally return empty and every **
write**\n> — creating a persona or goal, launching a run, publishing a study,\n> requesting insights — answers `403` with a messag

e naming the feature, not a
> `404` and not a validation error.
>
> Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because
every one of them\n> *reduces* exposure and spend: cancelling a goal run, unpublishing a\n> study, and archiving a persona, goal o
r swarm (each one's `DELETE`). An\n> organization that loses access can still stop what is running and clean up\n> what it authore

d.
>
> Ask us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you want it turned on.

**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{proje
ctId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,\n`.../swarms...`) — the definitions a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthet
ic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made\

nunder it. Nothing here starts anything — launching is
`POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\
n| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |\n| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `
GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so
renaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../
goals` | List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` mus
t be in this project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `envi
ronmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing ru
ns keep pointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a s
warm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update
the container's defaults. Not a cascade — existing goals keep their own values |\n| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a
